recipes.name: Red curry chicken & squash, ginger and lime
recipes.note: Adapted from FOOBY: more squash, less coconut milk, plus ginger and lime. Four-portion quantities; onion and paste weights and the 35-minute total are estimates.
recipes.method:
Soften sliced onion, diced squash and grated ginger in the oil for 3 minutes. Stir in rice and curry paste.
Add bouillon and coconut milk; cover and simmer about 15 minutes until the rice and squash are nearly tender.
Season thin chicken strips with salt, add and gently simmer until cooked through, about 5–8 minutes. Finish with lime zest and juice, coriander and chilli.

recipes.name: Salmon & leek linguine, miso-yoghurt sauce
recipes.note: Adapted from FOOBY: extra leek and salmon, smaller pasta and cheese portions. Honey, miso and lemon conversions are approximate; source timing retained.
recipes.method:
Cook linguine until just tender, reserving 200 ml cooking water per original four-portion batch.
Sauté leeks in half the oil for 5–8 minutes; briefly add garlic. Stir in honey, miso and reserved water and simmer 2 minutes. Fold in pasta, then yoghurt, Cheddar and lemon juice over gentle heat.
Season salmon with salt and pepper and pan-fry in remaining oil, roughly 3 minutes per side depending on thickness, until cooked. Serve over the leeks and pasta.

recipes.name: Dill pork meatballs, mustard gravy & celeriac mash
recipes.note: Adapted from Lulu Grimes / Good Food using chicken bouillon, Dijon and nutmeg, with added celeriac-potato mash and beans. Side quantities and 45-minute timing are estimates.
recipes.method:
Boil diced celeriac and potato until tender, about 20 minutes; drain and mash with warm milk and some salt. Steam the green beans.
Mix pork, egg, grated onion, breadcrumbs, half the dill, nutmeg and pepper; shape small balls. Brown in oil in batches.
Remove the meatballs. Cook flour in butter for 2 minutes, whisk in chicken stock and Dijon, then simmer with the meatballs until cooked throughout. Finish with remaining dill; serve with mash, beans and preserve.

recipes.name: Saffron fish stew, fennel, orange & mint
recipes.note: Adapted from Williams Sonoma with fish bouillon replacing clam juice and extra fennel and fish. Metric conversions are approximate; source 45-minute prep plus 45-minute cook retained.
recipes.method:
Bloom saffron in 30 ml hot water per original batch for 20 minutes. Soften shallot and chilli in half the oil; add stock, wine, thyme, bay, orange peel, fennel seed, remaining water and saffron. Simmer 10 minutes, then strain.
Sauté fennel wedges, pepper strips and onion in remaining oil. Add strained broth, salt and pepper and simmer 10 minutes. Nestle in fish and poach gently until opaque, about 10 minutes.
Remove bay and peel if any remain. Off heat, temper sour cream with a little broth and stir back in. Finish with chopped mint; reserve the orange flesh for another use.

recipes.name: Ginger chicken & chestnuts, shiitake and star anise
recipes.note: Adapted from Charmaine Katz / Waitrose: sherry and one soy sauce, added pak choi and rice. Estimated 75 minutes includes a 30-minute mushroom soak; allow 30 minutes extra if needed.
recipes.method:
Soak shiitake in the measured hot water for 30–60 minutes until soft, reserving the liquid. Meanwhile coat chicken in half the sherry, some soy, salt and white pepper; refrigerate while soaking.
Fry spring-onion whites, garlic, ginger and star anise in 15 ml oil per original batch. Brown chicken, then add mushrooms, strained soaking liquid and remaining sherry and soy. Simmer 10 minutes; add cooked chestnuts and simmer 8–10 minutes until chicken is cooked.
Cook rice separately and stir-fry pak choi in remaining oil. Remove star anise and finish the braise with spring-onion greens.

recipes.name: Harissa savoy cabbage, butter beans & baked feta
recipes.note: Adapted from Esther Clark / Good Food Middle East. Drained beans, paste, rind and garnish weights estimated. The 45-minute estimate allows the method’s 15 + 20 minute oven stages and preparation.
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200°C conventional / 180°C fan. Coat savoy wedges with half the oil, ras el hanout and salt; roast 15 minutes.
Mix drained butter beans, tomatoes, harissa, preserved-lemon rind and sugar; pour around the cabbage. Put feta on a separate lined tray with most remaining oil and chilli. Roast both for another 20 minutes, until cabbage is tender.
Serve cabbage and beans with chunks of feta. Finish with parsley, dill and the last drizzle of oil.

recipes.name: Dukkah-crusted chicken, celeriac, dates & green olives
recipes.note: Adapted from FOOBY. Uses homemade dukkah and honey in place of the date syrup, with less dried fruit and a smaller portion of bone-in thighs. Quantities and timing are estimates.
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200°C. Toast hazelnuts and sesame, then crush coarsely with cumin and ground coriander. Stir half the mixture into lime juice, honey, olive oil and salt.
Set aside some glaze for celeriac wedges. Dust chicken in flour, brush with the remaining glaze and press into a mixture of panko and the reserved dry dukkah. Arrange with the glazed celeriac on a wide lined tray.
Roast 25 minutes, then tuck the chopped dates and green olives around the celeriac. Roast another 10–15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the wedges are tender. Spoon the date and olive juices over the vegetables.

recipes.name: Tarragon chicken & leeks with lemon pan jus
recipes.note: Adapted from Nigel Slater in The Observer. Uses boneless breasts, less oil and a little lemon zest. Leek weight and wine volume are estimates.
recipes.method:
Pat the chicken dry, season it and brown it on both sides in olive oil. Transfer it to a plate while you wash and slice the leeks.
Sweat the leeks in the same pan, covered, until silky. Add the wine and scrape up the browned bits, then pour in the stock and return the chicken. Simmer until the meat is cooked through and the sauce lightly coats a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat. Add chopped tarragon, lemon zest and enough lemon juice to brighten the sauce.

recipes.name: Sage pork steaks, caramelised apples & mustard cabbage
recipes.note: Adapted from Good Food. Adds savoy cabbage in place of a starchy side and more stock to cook the greens. Produce weights and adapted timing are estimates.
recipes.method:
Season the pork and sear on both sides in a wide oiled pan. Transfer to a plate. Brown apple wedges and sliced onion in the same pan, then add torn sage and shredded savoy.
Stir Dijon into the stock and pour it into the pan. Simmer until the cabbage is tender and the liquid starts to thicken. Return the pork and any juices and finish cooking it gently.
Rest the steaks briefly while the sauce reduces to a light glaze. Spoon the apples, sage and mustard cabbage over the pork.

recipes.name: Crisp sea bass, orange broccoli & anchovy-caper dressing
recipes.note: Adapted from Gordon Ramsay’s Good Food recipe with less oil and capers. Broccoli and drained garnish weights are estimates. Buy scaled, skin-on fillets.
recipes.method:
Cut the orange into segments and squeeze the trimmings into a bowl. Blanch the broccoli for 1–2 minutes, drain well and char briefly in a hot pan. Toss with the orange segments, juice and a splash of oil.
Pat the fish dry and season lightly. Sear skin-side down in oil for about 3–4 minutes, pressing it flat briefly. Flip and cook until just done, about 1–2 minutes depending on thickness.
Sizzle the drained capers and chopped anchovies in the remaining oil. Take off the heat, add lemon zest and juice, and spoon around the fish so the skin stays crisp.

recipes.name: Sherry-glazed cod, parsnip mash & garlicky spinach
recipes.note: Adapted from Jennifer Joyce’s Good Food recipe. Uses parsnips, adds spinach and skips the chilli. Adapted quantities are estimates.
recipes.method:
Boil diced parsnips until tender, about 12–15 minutes. Drain well, then mash with butter, chopped parsley and part of the salt and pepper.
Dust seasoned cod with flour. Pan-sear in olive oil until the fish flakes easily, turning once. Set aside. Wilt the spinach with one sliced garlic clove and a little oil, then divide among plates.
Sizzle the rest of the garlic in the fish pan. Stir in sherry vinegar and brown sugar and reduce to a syrupy glaze. Spoon it over the cod and serve with the mash, spinach and lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Harissa pumpkin & crisp chickpeas with lime tahini
recipes.note: Adapted from Ottolenghi’s pumpkin side. Adds drained tinned chickpeas and sesame for a main, with less harissa and brown sugar in place of maple syrup. Adapted timing and garnish weights are estimates.
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss bite-size pumpkin pieces with most of the oil, crushed garlic, salt and pepper. Put harissa on some or all of the pieces to suit your table. Roast for about 30–35 minutes, turning once.
Dry the drained chickpeas, toss with the remaining oil and roast on a second tray for about 25 minutes, until crisp at the edges. Add the sesame for the final 3 minutes.
Whisk tahini with soy, lime juice and brown sugar, loosening it with a splash of water. Serve the pumpkin and chickpeas with the sauce, sliced spring onions and coriander.

recipes.name: Harissa chicken, roast squash & lemon yoghurt
recipes.note: Adapted from Good Food (4.6/5, 78 ratings; recipe describes a low-calorie version). The published recipe scales from four; squash and onion quantities are approximate and lemon-mint yoghurt is an added finish.
recipes.method:
Heat the oven to 200°C. Mix most of the harissa with half the yoghurt and coat the chicken; season. Toss squash and onion with the remaining harissa, olive oil and salt, then roast for 10 minutes.
Add chicken to the tray and roast 20–25 minutes more, turning the vegetables once, until chicken is cooked and squash is browned.
Stir lemon zest and juice with the remaining yoghurt and chopped mint. Serve as a cool, sharp sauce.

recipes.name: Salmon, leeks & winter greens in chive crème fraîche
recipes.note: Adapted from Good Food (4.7/5, 154 ratings). More leeks and greens, smaller crème fraîche portion, lemon finish; chicken stock is suitable for this family recipe.
recipes.method:
Soften sliced leeks in a little oil for 8 minutes. Add stock and simmer until reduced slightly; stir in crème fraîche, lemon zest and pepper.
Add peas and broad beans, nestle salmon in the pan, cover and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes, depending on thickness, until just cooked.
Scatter with snipped chives and lemon juice. Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer so it stays silky.

recipes.name: Mustard pork, braised red cabbage, pears & walnuts
recipes.note: Adapted from Good Food (4.6/5, 5 ratings). Scale and seasoning amounts are estimates; add walnuts at the end for crunch and use vegetable bouillon for the cabbage.
recipes.method:
Shred cabbage and simmer covered with pear wedges, grated ginger, vegetable stock and balsamic vinegar for about 40 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in half the chopped walnuts.
Brush pork fillet with oil and wholegrain mustard; grill or sear, turning, until just cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Taste the cabbage for acidity and seasoning. Serve with the pork and finish with remaining walnuts and parsley.

recipes.name: Mustard-glazed trout, fennel & herby potato salad
recipes.note: Adapted from Good Food (4.7/5, 14 ratings). Reduce the potato portion and use modest sour cream; fresh trout is a Coop-friendly substitute where available.
recipes.method:
Boil potatoes until just tender. Toss thinly sliced onion and fennel with lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Mix mustard, honey, half the lemon zest and oil for the glaze.
Brush trout with the glaze and bake at 200°C for about 10 minutes, until just opaque and flaking.
Fold sliced potatoes with sour cream, chopped dill and parsley, remaining zest and the quick-pickled fennel and onion. Serve with the trout.

recipes.name: Pork medallions, caramelised apples & sage mustard sauce
recipes.note: Adapted from Good Food (4.6/5, 50 ratings; 246 kcal per source serving). Adds a pile of quick wilted cabbage; timings depend on medallion thickness.
recipes.method:
Sear pork medallions in half the oil for about 2 minutes per side; remove to a plate. Add apple wedges and cook until golden and tender, about 8–10 minutes.
Add stock and mustard, simmer until lightly reduced, then return pork with chopped sage and cook gently until just cooked through.
Stir crème fraîche into the sauce off the heat. Quickly wilt shredded cabbage in remaining oil with a splash of water; serve alongside.

recipes.name: Winter lentil soup, leek, celery & lemon-thyme yoghurt
recipes.note: Adapted and doubled from Good Food (4.2/5, 110 ratings; 264 kcal per source serving). Adds a lemon-thyme yoghurt swirl and parsley; quantities are approximate for four.
recipes.method:
Soften diced carrot, celery and leek in olive oil. Stir in tomato purée, chopped garlic and ground coriander for 1 minute.
Add rinsed red lentils and vegetable bouillon; simmer 25–30 minutes until lentils and vegetables are tender. Blend about a third for a thicker, rustic texture.
Mix yoghurt with lemon zest and thyme leaves. Season the soup with lemon juice and pepper, then finish each bowl with the yoghurt and parsley.
